_comment: Illustrative, high-level rule summaries used as grounding context for the test harness. Edit freely. They are NOT legal advice and are not exhaustive; verify with counsel before relying on any verdict in production.

DE.name: Germany
notes: Weapons Act (WaffG) bans knuckle dusters, switchblades/automatic knives, butterfly knives and similar; ordinary fixed-blade and folding knives are legal to sell.
Pepper spray may only be sold when labelled as an animal-repellent spray (Tierabwehrspray); sprays marketed for use against people are not permitted.
Hemp/CBD products are permitted up to 0.3% THC; higher THC content falls under narcotics law.
Kratom is not a scheduled narcotic but is an unauthorised novel food, so it may not be sold for consumption.
Nicotine pouches (tobacco-free) are treated as unauthorised food and may not be sold; vapes and e-liquids are legal, max 20 mg/ml nicotine and 2 ml tank, adults only.
Alcohol including absinthe is legal to sell to adults; thujone limits apply under EU rules (35 mg/kg for strong spirits).
Laser pointers above class 2 (1 mW) may not be sold to consumers.
Ivory trade is prohibited except antiques with valid CITES/EU documentation.
Prescription medicines (e.g. tramadol) require a prescription and licensed pharmacy; melatonin above about 1 mg is treated as a medicine.
Hydroquinone is banned in cosmetics across the EU; SARMs are not approved for human use.
Real-money online gambling requires a German GGL licence.

UK.name: United Kingdom
notes: Flick knives, butterfly knives, disguised knives and knuckle dusters are banned; selling any knife to under-18s is illegal.
Pepper spray is classed as a prohibited weapon (Firearms Act s.5) and cannot be sold.
Kratom is covered by the Psychoactive Substances Act 2016, so supply for human consumption is illegal.
CBD products need FSA novel-food authorisation and must have no more than trace controlled cannabinoids (1 mg per container).
Single-use disposable vapes are banned from sale since 1 June 2025; refillable vapes allowed with max 20 mg/ml nicotine and 2 ml tank.
Nicotine pouches are legal to sell to adults.
Melatonin is prescription-only.
Prescription medicines (e.g. tramadol, Class C controlled) require a prescription.
Hydroquinone is banned in cosmetics; SARMs are unlicensed medicines and cannot be sold for human use.
Ivory Act 2018 bans dealing in elephant ivory with narrow exemptions requiring registration.
Real-money gambling requires a UK Gambling Commission licence.
Laser pointers above 1 mW should not be sold to consumers (product safety guidance).

US.name: United States (federal baseline; state law varies)
notes: Switchblades cannot be shipped across state lines (Federal Switchblade Act); knuckle dusters are illegal in several states.
Pepper spray is legal in most states with size limits in some.
Hemp-derived CBD is federally legal at or below 0.3% delta-9 THC.
Kratom is federally unscheduled but banned in several states (e.g. Alabama, Arkansas, Indiana, Rhode Island, Vermont, Wisconsin).
Vapes and e-liquids need FDA premarket authorisation; most flavoured disposables are unauthorised. Nicotine products are 21+.
Melatonin is sold over the counter.
Tramadol is Schedule IV and prescription-only; selling without a prescription is a federal offence.
Hydroquinone is prescription-only since 2020 (no OTC sale); SARMs cannot be sold as dietary supplements.
Laser pointers above 5 mW cannot legally be marketed as pointers (FDA).
Near-total ban on elephant ivory sales with narrow antique exemptions.
Online casino gambling is legal only in a handful of states with a licence.

IN.name: India
notes: E-cigarettes, vapes and e-liquids are fully banned (PECA 2019); import, sale and advertising are offences.
Cannabis flower and resin (including THC-rich CBD extracts) are controlled under the NDPS Act; some hemp products are permitted under state licences.
Tramadol has been a scheduled psychotropic under NDPS since 2018 and requires a prescription.
Real-money online gaming (casino, betting) is banned nationwide under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025.
Ivory trade is banned under the Wildlife (Protection) Act.
Alcohol sale is state-licensed and cannot be sold online in most states.
Knuckle dusters and concealed weapons fall under the Arms Act.
Melatonin and many supplements are sold OTC but hydroquinone above 2% is prescription-only.

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
notes: Any cannabis or THC content, including CBD oils, is prohibited under narcotics law; kratom is also banned.
Alcohol can only be sold by licensed outlets to licence holders; online sale by general merchants is not permitted.
Vapes and nicotine products are legal but must meet ESMA standards and are sold to adults only.
Pepper spray, knuckle dusters and most self-defence weapons are prohibited.
Tramadol is a controlled substance and requires a prescription; SARMs and hydroquinone products are restricted.
Gambling is illegal except for operators licensed by the GCGRA.
Ivory and CITES-listed wildlife products are banned.
Counterfeit goods are seized and sellers prosecuted.
